ordered_diagnoses: Rickettsial disease with central nervous system involvement

facts.raw_span: A 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
altered mental status
febrile and intermittently responsive (Glasgow Coma Scale 10)
left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology was positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT demonstrated a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect but no hemorrhage
Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema
Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
no valvular vegetations
Repeat lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 30 cm H₂O, 1762 WBCs/mm³
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement

concepts.why: The patient has a history of intravenous heroin use, which increases the risk of infective endocarditis, and presents with fever, altered mental status, and cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis, suggesting central nervous system infection.

The patient has a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity on brain MRI, consistent with a brain abscess, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows pleocytosis and elevated protein.

The patient has a history of intravenous heroin use and benzodiazepine and opiate positivity on urine toxicology, which can cause toxic leukoencephalopathy, and presents with altered mental status and limb weakness.

The patient has a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity on brain MRI, consistent with vasculitis, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows pleocytosis and elevated protein.
The patient has a history of hepatitis C, which can cause hepatic encephalopathy, and presents with altered mental status.

concepts.preferred_label: Rickettsial disease with central nervous system involvement
concepts.why: The patient presents with fever and altered mental status, and has a history of intravenous heroin use, which increases the risk of rickettsial disease.

The patient has a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity on brain MRI, consistent with PML, and has a history of immunosuppression due to hepatitis C.

The patient has a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on head CT, which could be consistent with a cerebral hemorrhage, although the absence of hemorrhage on imaging makes this less likely.

The repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement, which is consistent with the development of a brain abscess.

rationales.F01: Hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use may increase the risk of certain infections, but the relationship to the current presentation is unclear.
rationales.F03: Fever is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in various conditions, including infections and inflammatory diseases.
rationales.F05: Leukocytosis is a non-specific finding that can be seen in various conditions, including infections and inflammatory diseases.
rationales.F07: The absence of hemorrhage on head CT makes cerebral hemorrhage less likely.
rationales.F10: The absence of valvular vegetations on echocardiography makes subacute bacterial endocarditis less likely.
